description: Modern deep learning from the building blocks up: layers, activations and automatic differentiation, training deep networks reliably, convolutional networks for vision, recurrent networks for sequences, attention and transformers, generative models from autoencoders to diffusion, and transfer learning when compute and data are scarce. Every architecture is built from tensors in PyTorch, trained in the browser lab on small budgets and then scaled up, with experiments on African data such as crop disease images and local-language text.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning
Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola, Dive into Deep Learning
Bishop and Bishop, Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts
outcomes: Build neural networks from layers, activations and loss functions and implement automatic differentiation for them.
Train deep networks reliably using suitable initialisation, normalisation, optimisers and regularisation, and diagnose training failures.
Design and train convolutional networks for image classification, detection and segmentation.
Model sequences with recurrent networks and with attention-based transformers, and explain their trade-offs.
Implement and evaluate generative models including autoencoders, GANs and diffusion models.
Adapt pretrained models with transfer learning, fine-tuning and compression to work under limited compute and data.

units.title: Neural network building blocks
topics: From linear models to multilayer perceptrons; depth, width and universal approximation
Activation functions: sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and their gradients
Loss functions: mean squared error, cross-entropy and their probabilistic interpretation
Computational graphs and reverse-mode automatic differentiation implemented from scratch
Tensors, broadcasting and GPU computation in PyTorch; modules, datasets and data loaders

units.title: Training deep networks
topics: Initialisation schemes: Xavier and He; vanishing and exploding gradients
Normalisation: batch, layer and group normalisation; residual connections
Optimisers: SGD with momentum, Adam and AdamW; learning-rate schedules and warm-up
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, label smoothing and early stopping
Double descent and generalisation in over-parameterised networks
Debugging training: overfitting a small batch, loss curves, gradient norms and experiment tracking

units.title: Convolutional networks
topics: Convolution, padding, stride, pooling and receptive fields; parameter sharing and equivariance
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and efficient networks such as MobileNet and EfficientNet
Object detection and semantic segmentation: anchor boxes, YOLO-style detectors and U-Net
Visualising and interpreting CNNs: saliency maps and Grad-CAM
Classifying cassava and cocoa leaf diseases from smartphone photographs

units.title: Recurrent networks and sequences
topics: Sequence modelling tasks; recurrent neural networks and backpropagation through time
Long short-term memory and gated recurrent units; gradient clipping
Bidirectional and stacked RNNs; sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder models
Word embeddings and tokenisation for low-resource languages such as Twi, Ewe and Hausa

units.title: Attention and transformers
topics: Attention as soft lookup; scaled dot-product and multi-head attention
The transformer: positional encodings, encoder and decoder blocks, layer normalisation and feed-forward layers
Pretraining objectives: masked language modelling and next-token prediction; BERT and GPT-style models
Vision transformers and multimodal models in brief
Scaling laws, efficient attention and the cost of large models
Building a small transformer for machine translation between English and a Ghanaian language

units.title: Generative models
topics: Autoencoders and variational autoencoders: the evidence lower bound and the reparameterisation trick
Generative adversarial networks: the minimax game, training instability and mode collapse
Normalising flows in brief
Diffusion models: forward noising, denoising score matching and sampling
Autoregressive language models and decoding strategies: greedy, beam search, top-k and nucleus sampling
Evaluating generative models and the risks of synthetic media and deepfakes

units.title: Transfer learning with limited compute
topics: Feature extraction versus fine-tuning; choosing layers to freeze
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning: adapters and LoRA
Self-supervised and contrastive pretraining; few-shot learning with foundation models
Model compression: quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation
Mixed precision, gradient accumulation and free or shared GPUs; on-device inference for low-bandwidth users

units.title: Responsible deployment and capstone
topics: Dataset bias, under-representation of African data and fairness evaluation
Robustness, adversarial examples and distribution shift
Serving a model and monitoring it after deployment; energy and environmental cost
Capstone: a deep learning project on an African dataset with a model card and compute budget report
